items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: The interviewee mentions Bechet only in the interviewer's question as a comparison for tone style ('might have related to Bechet') and does not claim any personal interaction, meeting, or direct musical relationship with Bechet.

ctx.x: Well, Rod Kless told me that he consciously imitated Johnny Dodds, and that he was a great influence on him, which was hard for me to understand. My heroes were Larry Shields and Rapolo. But they weren't Tesh, I'm quite sure. They certainly weren't Rods. And of course, Goodman would be the only exception to my age group, because Goodman was quite a bit younger. And you can find records of Goodman's, or rather, test records, some of which have been repeated, with the Pollock Band, Unreleased Masters, where Benny…

That influence kept bobbing up, even into the 30s, and thinned out soon after when it became more respectable for pure tone. But I've wondered whether Tesh, finding the raspy and the hard tone so full of emotion, might have related to Bechet or to Dodds, who were so capable in using the expressive distortion of tone. And to say that it probably was a sequence isn't quite as accurate as knowing that it was. And so this question will continue to bob up.
The one who probably can answer it, of course, is Pee Wee. And Pee Wee probably could give you a very clear-cut answer on that.
